kw.doc: Open the emulator bench: build the OpenRTX Linux emulator for the radio file's mic_chain model (its CONFIG_MIC_* values) and the variant's defines, ready to send test signals through its M17 microphone chain. `firmware` is <variant>@<OpenRTX commit>, checked against the checkout. kw.name: Measure Static Level Curve
Mic Chain Should Meet Limit
kw.doc: Fail unless summary[field] is at most the radio file's mic_chain.limits[limit]. A figure that couldn't be measured (a release that never settled) fails.

test.doc: 1 kHz and 400 Hz tones over the ADC's range: the level into codec2 and out of it against the input, beside the codec-only reference. Nothing may reach full scale before codec2.

test.name: Speech Level Sweep

kw.name: Measure Speech Level Sweep
kw.doc: Speech files (default the four Harvard-sentence recordings in SPEECH_DIR) at each ADC peak level: active level, peak, onset, clipping and STOI, before and after codec2, with the codec-only references. Returns the level spread over the input range, the STOI deficit against the ideal reference and the worst clipping.

test.name: Key-up Onset

kw.name: Measure Key-up Onset
kw.doc: The key-up transient: the peak of the first 100 ms of every speech take, before and after codec2. Uses the speech sweep's takes, running them first when this run hasn't.

kw.name: Mic Chain Should Meet Limit
kw.doc: Fail unless summary[field] is at most the radio file's mic_chain.limits[limit]. A figure that couldn't be measured (a release that never settled) fails.

test.doc: The transient at key-up, the first 100 ms of every speech take, before codec2: the DC block's start must not click.

test.name: Listening-Condition Intelligibility

kw.name: Measure Listening Intelligibility
kw.doc: The speech sweep's decoded audio as a listener hears it at a fixed receiver volume: at its own level, with pink noise at each level (dBFS RMS of full scale) added, scored with STOI against the clean source, beside the codec-only references under the same conditions. No new emulator runs: the sweep's takes are re-scored (and run first, from the cache, when this run hasn't). Returns the mean, the worst cell and the worst deficit against the ideal reference.

kw.name: Mic Chain Should Meet Limit
kw.doc: Fail unless summary[field] is at most the radio file's mic_chain.limits[limit]. A figure that couldn't be measured (a release that never settled) fails.

test.doc: The speech sweep's decoded audio as a listener hears it at a fixed receiver volume, at its own level with pink noise added: STOI normalises level, so only here does a quiet talker buried at the listener count against the chain. In every cell of input and noise level the chain should come within the limit of the codec-only ideal reference (the same input, ideally processed to -21 dBFS active). Re-scores the sweep's takes; no new emulator runs.

kw.name: Measure Silence Gate
kw.doc: Speech bursts and pauses over a pink noise bed at each level (dBFS RMS of the ADC range): the level in the pauses, its drift within a pause (noise pumping) and the speech-to-pause ratio.

kw.name: Close Bench
kw.doc: Stop the instruments and write measurements.json: every capture, check and operator answer, with the run's provenance. Absolute paths are made relative, so the file can be published as it is.

suite.doc:
The M17 microphone chain, on the emulator bench: test signals shaped by the radio file's mic_chain model (oversampling, gain, ADC) go through the OpenRTX Linux emulator's real encodeFunc, codec2 and M17 modulator; the decoded voice and the samples codec2 was given (the firmware's pre-codec tap) are measured. The firmware is one variant of an OpenRTX checkout, built with that radio's CONFIG_MIC_* values.
Limits are the radio file's mic_chain.limits: the target of the microphone-chain change, which today's fixed-gain chain is expected to miss. The method, the signals and the metrics are in docs/emulator-mic-campaign.md, which each run keeps as METHODS.md next to its tables and charts.
Run it with bench/emulator.args; it needs the emulator bench, so other benches exclude it (needs:emulator).
